fixed_statement:
Assumptions / Conditions / Definitions.
- Let \(I(V_{\{1\}})=\{x\in \Dr_1\mid x\subset V_{\{1\}}\}\).
- Let \(F(V_{L_1})=\{T\in \Dr_2\mid V_{L_1}\subset T\}\).
- Let \(\Phi\) be as in Lemma 3.1.

Statement :
The map \(\Phi\) gives a bijection
\[
I(V_{\{1\}})\longleftrightarrow F(V_{L_1}).
\]
\[
|F(V_{L_1})|=\mathfrak c.
\]
fixed_proof: By Proposition 1, \(\Phi\) maps \(\Dr_1\) bijectively to \(\Dr_2\). Lemma 3.1 gives exactly the containment equivalence defining the ideal \(I(V_{\{1\}})\) and the filter \(F(V_{L_1})\). Proposition 2 gives \(|I(V_{\{1\}})|=\mathfrak c\). Since \(|I(V_{\{1\}})|=\mathfrak c\), it follows that \(|F(V_{L_1})|=\mathfrak c\).
reason: Moved the cardinality derivation from the statement into the proof, while keeping the bijection and final cardinality claim in the statement. No outside text was needed.
